title: Albert Einstein: the 1905 Annalen papers, the dissertation, the general theory of 1915–1917, and the Gemeinverständlich

license.payload: Per item, recorded in origin.items. Every work was first published 1905–1920 and is in the public domain in the United States (published before 1931, the term of 95 years run). Einstein died in 1955: the term of life plus seventy years ran out at the end of 2025, so the works are also free in the European Union and in other countries of that term from 2026-01-01; a country with a longer term may still hold them, for example Spain, where authors who died before 1987 have life plus eighty years, to the end of 2035. The Annalen der Physik scans are the Internet Archive's microfilm series (collection sim_microfilm); the items carry no rights or licence field, and the Archive names the journal's present publisher, Wiley. The Sitzungsberichte 1915 volume (Google scan uploaded by ARLIMA) and the Vieweg book of 1920 (Google scan) carry the Public Domain Mark 1.0. The Sitzungsberichte 1917 volume is a Digital Library of India scan with no rights field. The three Wikisource pages are CC BY-SA 4.0 for the site's contributions.
license.record: CC-BY-4.0 applies to this seat record only.

normalization: Originals as fetched under original/. text/<slug>.ocr.txt is the Internet Archive's OCR layer (_djvu.txt) with line endings normalized; text/<slug>.txt is the Wikisource parser output reduced by code. Five Annalen issues, the 1916 Annalen issue and the Sitzungsberichte 1915 volume are held by reference (identifier, file, size and the md5 the Archive publishes); their OCR layers are copied. No text was corrected by hand.
units: one text file per witness; an issue or volume that carries other papers is seated whole, and the work description names the pages of Einstein's paper

scope: Held: the five papers of 1905 and 1906 named in the ruling (the light-quantum paper, Brownian motion, the electrodynamics of moving bodies, the inertia of energy, and the dissertation as printed in the Annalen), the field equations of 25 November 1915 with the three November papers that share its volume, the Grundlage of 1916, the cosmological paper of 1917, and the popular book in its fifth printing of 1920. The Annalen issues are the Internet Archive's microfilm series: each issue scan carries many papers, so the issue is seated whole and each work names its pages. German Wikisource has proofread transcriptions of three of the papers (Elektrodynamik, Trägheit, Feldgleichungen), seated as second text layers; it has none of the others. Not held: the first printing of 1917 of the Gemeinverständlich, which the Archive does not hold (the 1920 fifth printing is held twice, as bub_gb_kTdWAAAAMAAJ and berdiespezielle00unkngoog, the same Wisconsin copy scanned by Google; the first is seated). The 1905 dissertation as separately printed in Bern (Wyss, 1905) was not found on the Archive.
why_seated: The year 1905 is the hinge of the exact sciences in the twentieth century, and its five papers are short enough to be read whole in the issues that first carried them. The seat holds each in the scan of its first printing, with the pages named, so that a reader can pass from a formula cited anywhere to the page it came from. The general theory follows in the same way, from the Academy's half-year volumes to the Annalen of 1916, and the popular book closes the seat in Einstein's own plain words.
